verdict: Core same-member-all-rivals and actual repair/harm calculations are sound; supplemental interpretation risks require explicit reporting.

findings.issue: Added fields omit the baseline-wrong condition; a floating-point common-rival/pool-correct coincidence makes them candidate-correct counts.
findings.handling: Preserve sealed values, add notice, report candidate-correct/kept-correct separately from strict paired repairs in a separate successor.

findings.issue: Newly common classes are counted only on original COMMON-obstruction objects; new obstructions outside that cohort are omitted.
findings.handling: Keep scoped labels; supply full-population new-common class/object counts separately and retain full repairs/harms.

findings.issue: Sealed route-permuted rank diagnostics use PERMUTED baseline rivals within COMMON-frozen cohorts; new adapter uses COMMON rivals for both candidate conditions.
findings.handling: Name anchor, cohort origin and transition; do not equate or subtract these into paired transition counts.

findings.issue: Numerical eligibility checks do not evaluate the separately frozen common-competitor mechanism statement.
findings.handling: Report desired mechanism independently; do not interpret numerical pass as mechanism success or change gates.

additional_limits: Old-rival reversals neither suffice for nor are necessary for actual pool repair
Strict rank criteria differ from native argmax ties
COMMON error-cohort improvement can coexist with full-population damage
Counters overlap; class-node and repeated seed-node counts are descriptive
Checkpoint selection uses the same development population
Pool-minus-member accuracy is accounting, not causal attribution
No topology, confirmation or broad competence claim follows
